title: On a compliance service the modal also takes the certificate
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in with View and edit customers, on the build under test. The Maintenance Reminders feature is on (maintenance_reminders flag).
  2. A service is due or overdue on an enrolled asset (e.g. 'PM-A' on unit 'ZZAUTOTEST Truck 12').
custom_steps:
1. Mark complete a compliance service.
  2. Confirm the modal also takes the certificate: number, Start date, End date and term.
  3. Confirm Start date defaults to the Reset date and End date fills from Start + term, both changeable.
  4. Close two compliance inspections on one work order and confirm details are asked per record.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • On a compliance service the modal also takes the certificate: number, Start date, End date and term.
  • Start date defaults to the Reset date, End date fills in from it plus the term, and both can be changed.
  • A work order closing two compliance inspections asks for details per record.
  • A compliance inspection's next due comes from the certificate's End date, not from the invoicing step's date list.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780 (Maintenance Reminders); story SV-10574 (S18, Complete a service and reset the cycle); Chunk 2 MR spec (Confluence 897679389), Part 1 / S18; read 2 Oct 2026. Source-verified 2 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S18-R5: “On a compliance service the modal also takes the certificate: number, Start date, End date and term, per S8-R10. Start date defaults to the Reset date, End date fills in from it plus the term, and both can be changed”
  • S18-E4: “A work order closing two compliance inspections asks for details per record”
  • S18-E6: “A compliance inspection is not in the step's list of dates. Its next due comes from the certificate's End date per S12-R4, entered in the certificate section of S18-R16”
